title: Superex Onion (Superex F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Superex onion is an F1 hybrid onion variety from Ramgo. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Superex onion is an F1 hybrid onion variety, also sold or known as Superex F1 or submarine sibuyas. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Ramgo.

heroImage.alt: Onion plants in beds separated by grassy paths on a Philippine farm, the kind of farm where Superex onion is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Superex F1 or submarine sibuyas, this is the same onion. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [onion variety finder](/crop-varieties/onion), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for onion and garlic](/land-preparation/onion-garlic-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: 80 to 90 days after transplanting (seller), a Nueva Ecija coop reports harvests from about 58 to 60 days. Yield, by the seller's count: 30 t/ha potential (seller). No trial on record checks these figures yet, so treat them as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit onion fields most often: [leafminer](/pests/leafminer), [onion armyworm](/pests/onion-armyworm), [purple blotch of onion](/diseases/purple-blotch), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** 80 to 90 days after transplanting (seller), a Nueva Ecija coop reports harvests from about 58 to 60 days.
**Fruit:** Yellow granex type: even globe bulbs with a double skin, yellow to yellow brown, thin closed neck.
Nicknamed the submarine onion for holding up through rainy spells.
Stands up to downy mildew, damping off and purple blotch (seller's claim).
Kept its colour after six months in storage.
Wanted by fast food buyers for burgers, onion rings and sauces.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: Agriculture Monthly called it the leading yellow granex onion in Nueva Ecija, it made up 60 percent of the onions a San Jose City coop sold as white onions, Ramgo showcases it as a bestseller. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual onion on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Superex onion

Red onion stores longer, while yellow onion yields more. Pick a variety that bulbs in the short days of the Philippine dry season, and plant it after the rains so the bulbs dry well. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Superex F1 the same as Superex?
items.a: Yes. Superex F1 is another name for Superex. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Superex?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
